paragraphs: The bus left me at the edge of a [[rural]] county with two bags, a [[carry-on]], and a [[letter]] from my [[pater]] folded in my coat. The [[whole]] valley lay [[across]] a [[wide]] [[grassland]], and the road ran through it without a single [[curve]] for an hour. [[Here]] and there a house stood [[adjoining]] the old [[medieval]] [[bridge]], where a signpost helped me [[orient]] myself. I was [[actually]] more [[anxious]] than I admitted, and the [[visit]] began to [[seem]] a mistake. I [[deemed|deem]] it a [[difficult]] [[case]] from the first mile, though the driver only laughed at my [[certain]] frown. [[Each]] field looked the same, and I could not [[think]] of a [[good]] [[indication]] that I belonged here.

My [[vocation]] for the summer was to help [[remodel]] an old [[storehouse]] into a reading room for the local [[society]]. The [[interior]] smelled of [[paper]], dust, and the [[mixture]] of old [[goods]] that had been stored there for years. A [[volunteer]] [[instructor]] ran [[tuition]] classes in reading and [[mathematics]] for [[graduates|graduate]] who had never learned to read well. The programme was [[time-limited]], with a [[minimal]] budget and a [[non-standard]] daily [[routine]]. A [[leading]] [[unionist]] on the committee called the plan [[vital]] for the town's [[cultural]] life. We had no [[bandwidth]] yet, only one old [[tablet]] and a [[thermostat]] that could not decide between hot and cold.

On my first free afternoon I followed a [[pathway]] to the [[cave]] above the creek, [[curious]] about the paintings the children kept describing. An old [[prophet]] was said to have lived there, and a [[theology]] of storms had grown around his name until he was almost a [[god]]. The story was [[secular]] in [[origin]], yet it carried a strange [[holiness]], like a [[doctrine]] no church had ever [[formally]] accepted. The cave itself was almost [[unexplored]], and its [[theme]] was water: the ochre figures were barely [[visible]] in the dark. I began to [[fantasize]] that they were a kind of [[fiction]] written on rock, a story that could [[outlive]] us all, and I could not [[recollect]] who had first told me of it. There was [[grace]] in the way the light entered, and for an hour I felt something close to [[peace]].

A [[herd]] of [[wild]] horses still lived on the grassland, and a [[fierce]] stallion [[patrolled|patrol]] its edge. Their [[inborn]] and [[instinctive]] fear of people kept them at a distance. A [[mate]] stood beside the stallion, and the two [[fed|feed]] on [[grain]] scattered by the wind. A [[female]] vet took a [[swab]] from a young mare and, for the breeding programme, a blood sample. The county's [[measures|measure]] to protect the herd were [[timely]], and the vet [[encouraged|encourage]] us to keep the fence low. [[Beyond]] the fence a [[solvable]] problem waited: water in summer, shade in winter, and every [[animal]] watching us, even the [[cute]] foal.

My [[anxious]] nights had returned, the [[oppressive]] heat made my days [[unfocused]], and the [[therapy]] I had started in the city was now a phone call every Thursday. I took a [[tablet]] for [[fever]] on the third night, woke in [[sweat]] under a thick [[sweater]], and could not [[recover]] my breath. The doctor said the reaction was [[involuntary]] and did not mean I was [[unresponsive]] to treatment. I felt [[self-conscious]] about my [[awkward]] hands and [[embarrassed]] by the [[patient]] in the next bed, who never complained. It was an [[unpleasant]] [[degree]] of weakness, and I [[ought]] to have asked for help sooner. But the [[body]] has its own [[cunning]], every [[cell]] fighting in its own way, and by morning I felt almost [[normal]].

The town [[celebrated|celebrate]] its harvest with a [[custom]] older than the bridge: a tug-of-war [[match]] and a [[tune]] on the fiddle. A [[celebrity]] from the state capital came to open the fair, and the [[media]] followed her everywhere. Children [[whistled|whistle]] and [[swung|swing]] on ropes tied to the old oak, and the [[collective]] noise was [[noteworthy]]. The [[norm]] was that everyone brought a dish, and the [[mixture]] of [[vivid]] colours and smells was [[unimaginable]]. For one afternoon the town forgot its [[problems|problem]] and its [[biases|bias]], and even the [[good-natured]] arguments ended in laughter. I [[noted|note]] that the [[less]] people spoke about politics, the better the food tasted, and I bought a jar of [[herb]] honey for my pater.

In September a [[census]] taker came to the storehouse with a [[bilingual]] form and a long list of questions. The county wanted every [[voter]] registered before the [[congressional]] election, and the [[grassroots]] groups had begun a [[collective]] campaign. A [[union]] meeting in the hall argued that [[liberty]] without a [[paycheck]] was [[meaningless]]. The company's [[bid]] for the grassland had made [[homebuyers|homebuyer]] nervous and [[polarized|polarize]] the town. Its [[unilateral]] offer, made without the [[congress]], looked like a [[cunning]] move to [[govern]] the valley from outside, and the town wanted to [[minimize]] the damage. A [[mandatory]] [[measure]] would have [[bound|bind]] the county for thirty years, and the [[chair]] asked the council to [[seek]] advice. The council agreed to [[reconsider]], but the [[maximum]] the town could [[pay]] was small. The [[gross]] sum the company demanded was [[burdensome]] for a county of ten thousand people.

The only [[customer]] in the general store was a [[widow]] who bought [[goods]] at [[wholesale]] prices and sold them on, counting every coin from a worn [[pocketbook]]. She had [[hired|hire]] two graduates and paid them a [[paycheck]] that barely covered their [[tuition]] debts. Her [[energy]] was [[noteworthy]], and her [[field]] of knowledge was wider than the county line. A [[billion]] dollars of mining revenue had been promised, yet the county was already close to [[default]] on its loan. The whole town, she said, had been [[uninformed]] about the small print, and an unpaid [[bill]] had been [[cut]] from the budget.

In October a storm [[erupted|erupt]] over the ridge, the old man [[cursed|curse]] the sky, and a [[cascade]] of water came through the bridge. The creek became a [[seething]] brown flood, [[thick]] with mud and too fast to [[swim]], and the wind made the shutters [[rustle]]. We [[swept|sweep]] water from the reading room, [[coated|coat]] the shelves with oil, and [[diverted|divert]] the stream behind the shed. The storm was an [[indication]] of what the valley could expect, and our repairs were neither [[timely]] nor cheap. [[Unfortunately]], a [[letter]] from the county warned that the flood would [[degrade]] the land for years. The water had risen an [[inch]] above the floor, and the [[level]] of mud on the shelves told its own story.

That night a [[bang]] on the door woke us: someone had made an [[attack]] on the lock of the storehouse. The rumour spread that a bus had been [[hijacked|hijack]] at the depot, though an old poster spelled the word [[highjack]]. The [[suspect]] was a young man with a [[hip]] injury and no clear motive. The story was [[nonsense]], a [[meaningless]] rumour, but it [[sparked|spark]] a [[fierce]] argument on the steps. I had to [[defy]] the urge to leave and [[endure]] two hours of questions in the cold. The police [[suspended|suspend]] the inquiry, an [[investigator]] began to [[conduct]] interviews, and we locked the door [[lest]] someone return. The damage looked [[wilful]], even [[willful]], and I could [[swear]] the back door had been locked; the truth was not easy to [[erase]].

By then the town's [[gossip]] had turned me into a local figure, which was [[awkward]] for someone who disliked attention. A [[bias]] against outsiders could [[hinder]] every good idea, I learned, so I stopped arguing and started listening. The [[leading]] question at every meeting was whether the library was a [[hobby]] or a [[vocation]]. I learned to [[see]] the difference between a [[problem]] that was [[solvable]] and one that was merely [[unpleasant]]. [[Reasonableness]] was rare on both sides, [[cunning]] was common, and patience was rarer still. In the end the [[matter]] was settled by a [[few]] calm voices, not by the loudest ones.

The library opened in November as a [[center]] for learning, and a [[streaming]] line of readers began at nine and did not stop. A [[reader]] from the school took a [[paper]] bag home, and every book had a card [[attached|attach]] to the inside cover. A model [[orbiter]] above the blackboard seemed to [[sail]] through the room, and the children loved it. Our lending [[system]] was a notebook, a pencil, and one old [[tablet]] shared by everyone. The [[media]] came once, took photographs, and never returned, which was probably [[sensible]]. The [[thermostat]] failed again, so we moved into the [[centre]] of the room, where the old stove still worked, and we had to [[add]] a new heater in spring.

The company withdrew its bid in December, and the grassland stayed open. The [[legacy]] of that fight was a [[mandatory]] rule that any sale of public land must be voted on. A [[widow]] left the storehouse in her [[will]], with a [[note]] that it should always hold books. The [[reasonableness]] of that gift moved everyone, and the town [[converged|converge]] on the square to [[celebrate]] the [[renaissance]] of a building nobody had wanted. We had to [[reconstruct]] part of the roof and [[widen]] the door, and the work took [[less]] time than we feared. My therapy ended, my anxious nights grew rare, and I began to [[recover]] my old [[energy]]. I could [[think]] about the future without fear, which was a [[degree]] of peace I had not known for years. The company's [[defeat]] felt less like a victory than like a [[virtuous]] decision the whole town had made together; seasons [[cycled|cycle]], and for the first [[time]] I did not count them.

I still [[keep]] the notebook from that autumn, and I try to [[live]] by its plain advice. A place can be a [[paradise]] without being easy, and this one was both, [[thin]] soil and all. [[Beyond]] the county line the world was loud and [[unimaginable]], but I no longer feared it, and the cave, the herd and the bridge had become one [[mixture]] in my memory. [[Unfortunately]], I could not stay forever, and winter called me back to the city; I did not feel like a visitor [[anymore]]. But I [[won|win]] something there, and I [[mean]] to keep it. The [[end]] of that year was not an end at all, and the [[unfolding]] of the story would [[recur]] in my dreams for years.
